messages.content: Help me truncate the translog for a shard located at the path '/var/data/elasticsearch/nodes/0/indices/1shard', using the terminal interface for output and the index directory at '/var/data/elasticsearch/nodes/0/indices/1shard/index'?

function.name: TruncateTranslogAction_execute
function.description: Truncates the translog for a given shard path by creating a new empty checkpoint and translog file, and removes the existing translog files. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

terminal.description: The Terminal interface used for standard I/O interactions. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

shardPath.description: The ShardPath object representing the path to the shard whose translog needs to be truncated. ShardPath() constructor taking a Path object, which can be returned by  Paths.get(<path string>) for example This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

indexDirectory.description: The Directory object representing the path to the index directory of the shard. Directory object can be obtained by return value of FSDirectory.open a path string This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function TruncateTranslogAction_execute with parameters: terminal (string representation of Terminal interface), shardPath (string representation of ShardPath constructed from Path), indexDirectory (string representation of Directory). We need to provide strings that represent Java objects. For terminal, we can use "System.out" or something? The description says terminal: string, can be any type of Java object in string representation. So maybe "System.out". For shardPath: we need to construct ShardPath(Paths.get("/var/...")). So string representation could be "new ShardPath(Paths.get(\"/var/data/elasticsearch/nodes/0/indices/1shard\"))". For indexDirectory: FSDirectory.open(Paths.get(...)). So string representation: "FSDirectory.open(Paths.get(\"/var/data/elasticsearch/nodes/0/indices/1shard/index\"))". Let's produce JSON with those strings.

We should not include any other keys. Output must be valid JSON.
